assertions.text: Table uses value-set syntax (curly braces like {READ, WRITE} or {READ, WRITE, DELETE}) to express rules that hold across multiple actions
assertions.evidence: Table uses individual rows (ADMIN | READ | true, ADMIN | WRITE | true, etc.) without curly brace value-set syntax

assertions.text: Table has fewer than 9 data rows
assertions.evidence: Table contains exactly 9 data rows from 'Admin reads' through 'Guest cannot delete'

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Method body is: assertEquals(allowed, checker.canPerform(role, action));

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column is 'Scenario' with values like 'Admin reads', 'User writes', etc.

assertions.text: No two rows share both the same Role value and the same boolean output
assertions.evidence: ADMIN | READ | true, ADMIN | WRITE | true, ADMIN | DELETE | true share Role=ADMIN and Allowed=true

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title
assertions.evidence: Method is named 'checkPermission' which is generic; no @DisplayName annotation present

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it provides context beyond what the table rows already express
assertions.evidence: @Description is not present, and the assertion allows omission if table conveys context

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest
assertions.evidence: Only @TableTest is present; no ordering violations

assertions.text: If @Description is present and text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block
assertions.evidence: @Description is not present; assertion passes if absent

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Admin performs any action', 'Guest reads') — not outcomes ('Allowed', 'Denied')
assertions.evidence: Scenario names are 'Admin reads', 'User writes', 'Guest cannot write' describing conditions/actions
